name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +18 partisan lean
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at ~96%
Incumbent running in a seat Democrats hold comfortably
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Walkinshaw: an +18 Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a nearly 250-to-1 fundraising edge over Arthur Purves, who has almost no cash on hand. Markets price this at roughly 96% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise polling miss or unusually strong Republican turnout in a low-salience race could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District leans heavily Democratic, and first-term incumbent James Walkinshaw is seeking a full term after winning the seat. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, supplemented by substantial outside support. Republican Arthur Purves has raised only about $11,000 with $200 remaining, leaving him with little ability to communicate with voters. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable activity.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters list the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and resources. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 96% chance of winning. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the only open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
